question: Cryotherapy is an acceptable first-line ablative treatment for CIN 2 when the entire lesion is visible within the transformation zone, the endocervical canal is not involved, and invasive cancer has been excluded by biopsy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — this statement is true. Cryotherapy (and thermal ablation) are appropriate for CIN 2 meeting the 'see it all, biopsy says CIN' criteria. If there is any suspicion of invasion or unsatisfactory colposcopy, excision (LLETZ/LEEP) is required instead.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Cryotherapy is suitable for CIN 2 when colposcopy is satisfactory (entire lesion visible), the lesion fits within the cryoprobe, and biopsy has excluded invasion. These are the criteria for ablation vs excision.
